parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime layers a national universal-exposure document policy on top of a hostile division. At entry, every trans visitor faces the binary sex-marker regime, 'reasonable doubt' refusal mechanics with a potential lifetime fraud/misrepresentation bar, and documented confiscations stranding travellers — a state-engineered raising of discovery probability with no established remedy (litigation unresolved). Within the division, public-education and campus facilities follow assigned sex, statewide nondiscrimination protection is absent, hate-crime law excludes gender identity, and a criminalised care ban reaches an accompanying minor under 19. No violence incidents specific to the division are documented; the 3.8/100k figure is an undercount floor and carries no magnitude. Severe-but-narrower exposures than the 0.35 anchors' all-public-building and custodial rules, but clearly above unremedied-exclusion-free 0.55 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-marker passport policy, February 2025 cable directing refusal where 'reasonable doubt' on sex exists, fraud ground carrying possible permanent ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; civil-liberties litigation ongoing but unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate into fraud investigation and lifetime bar, then into detention/custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policies impose haircut rules, hormone removal; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Rescinded prison-protections order not restored; none documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor denied entry or investigated for fraud enters this custody system by birth sex or worse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division mandates birth-sex bathrooms in public schools, extension to colleges pending or assessed; SB 79 binary declaration; roughly half of jurisdictions nationally restrict facilities; state ID regime cannot be used by visitors but signals hostility.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented statewide; nationwide many jurisdictions unregulated.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor passing through educational or state buildings faces exclusion with no statewide recourse.

care_services.exposure: Class C felony for providers giving transition care to under-19s, enforceable since 2023; a travelling trans minor cannot continue medication; no statewide nondiscrimination or insurance protection.
care_services.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity but is marginal to care access.
care_services.interaction: Parent with trans minor risks child losing prescribed care; provider criminality deters any clinician.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official language frames gender identity as ideology and pro-trans positions as extremist-adjacent; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 'forbidden terms' policies.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders enjoined in court; rule-of-law contests ongoing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing raises probability and severity of any official encounter, from border to police stop.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban criminalises providers serving under-19s; national directives investigating schools and prosecuting facilitation of social transition; health-record subpoenas for under-19 patients.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care interruption and school/administrative scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans-visitor-specific violence in the division not documented; ID-congruence harassment documented circuit-wide via licence rules; 3.8/100k killing rate is an undercount floor with no magnitude value.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; circuit employment precedent only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police posture uncertain; hate-crime coverage excludes gender identity at state level.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide public-accommodations recourse; court posture in this circuit repeatedly denies document relief (Corbitt line); remedy litigation unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing suits and legal-aid FAQ resources; some neighbouring governments issue advisories.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight and courts have not produced operative relief for the exposures documented; unknowns (division violence, trespass enforcement here) unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A imposes a birth-sex rule on ALL public buildings with court-endorsed exclusion. Here the division's facility ban is narrower (education settings) and its trespass offence is not documented here, but the national entry/document regime adds a universal exposure 0.35-A lacks; net severity is comparable, slightly lower on facilities.

0.55-B has hostile operators but working mediators, no universal rules, and a conviction after assault. Here remedies do not operate against the operative rules, and the passport/entry regime is an unavoidable universal exposure absent in 0.55-B — materially harsher.

0.45-D features a universal unremedied security-search regime with accepting society. This dossier combines a comparable universal document/screening exposure with an actively hostile official climate, weakened state protections and a care ban for minors — somewhat worse, sitting between 0.35 and 0.45.

0.25-D adds recurrent police extortion stops and documented ward abuse on top of facility rules. This dossier documents state custody abuse nationally but no division-level extortion or arrest campaign, keeping it above 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces two stacked regimes: a national entry layer where sex-marker policy, reasonable-doubt refusals and fraud findings create continuous, unavoidable discovery probability with no working remedy, and a division layer of education-facility exclusion, no nondiscrimination law, no gender-identity hate-crime coverage and a criminalised minor-care ban. Interactions compound: a document mismatch can become a fraud investigation, detention in the documented abusive national custody system, or care denial for an accompanying minor. Protections are prospective (litigation, existing X passports) rather than operative. Divisions' unknowns (street violence, trespass enforcement here) are open questions, but the documented exposures place the jurisdiction in the high-elevated band.
